findings.title: Supported installers distribute commands without their required launcher
findings.reproduction: Confirmed all three. Both setup installers exit 0 from the --global branch before the runtime block. platforms/claude-code/install.sh - 7047 bytes, a third installer the implementer did not know existed - copies commands at line 90 and never writes runtime.json or bin/ap.py. A globally-installed command run in a project that was never project-installed fails with python's own "can't open file ... ap.py".
findings.resolution: ESCALATED TO THE HUMAN GATE. Not a repair: the fix requires choosing where a globally-installed command finds its launcher, which changes the shape of all 13 call sites and is inherited by the three adapters loops 004-005 will build. That is the same class of decision the loop-001-3 gate took, and the controller declines to take it unilaterally.

findings.title: /sync-install cannot repair the stale runtime it depends on
findings.reproduction: On a real scratch install: with a stale source_root, `ap.py install_audit` - step 2's own command - returns exit 3, for which step 2 documented no handling; with the launcher removed it returns exit 2, which step 2 treated as a configuration error and stopped on. The repair at 4b was unreachable in both cases it existed for.
findings.resolution: FIXED in fdc2ab9. The repair is now step 1b, ahead of the first launcher call, and step 2 documents exit 3 explicitly so it is never read as an audit verdict. Re-verified on the same install: both branches now reached. Revert-proven by test_the_guard_only_names_repairs_that_exist, which now asserts offset ordering rather than merely string presence - the exact weakness the reviewer named.

findings.title: Subdirectory reachability is masked by absolute-path testing
findings.reproduction: The relative invocation from a project subdirectory exits 2 with python's own "can't open file ... ap.py", before find_manifest() runs. The walk-up was inert as shipped.
findings.resolution: FIXED in fdc2ab9, by correcting the claim rather than the code. The test is renamed to what it actually proves - walk-up works for an ABSOLUTE launcher path - the real limit is pinned by its own test, and a second test asserts that no command changes directory before invoking the launcher. Contract 6 now states that commands run from the project root, consistent with every other path they name. The walk-up is retained, not removed: it is the route an out-of-project launcher would take, which is exactly what finding 1's decision may require.

findings.title: Valid JSON with the wrong shape bypasses the actionable guard
findings.reproduction: `[]` raised AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'; {"source_root": 1} raised AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'strip'. Both are raw tracebacks naming a launcher internal - precisely the failure mode the guard exists to replace.
findings.resolution: FIXED in fdc2ab9. The manifest is validated as an object with a string source_root; all four wrong shapes - [], {"source_root": 1}, a bare string, and null - now exit 3 naming the shape found, with no traceback. Revert-proven: removing the validation fails all four parametrised cases.
